claims.claim: Exact certificate characterization: G contains K6 minus an edge as an induced minor exactly when it has six pairwise-disjoint nonempty connected vertex sets A,B,C1,C2,C3,C4 such that A and B are anticomplete and every other pair of sets has an edge between it. Consequently detection is in NP and has an O(7^n n²) exact algorithm.
claims.evidence: This is precisely the branch-set definition of an induced minor when the only target nonedge is AB. Vertex deletion removes unused vertices, contractions collapse the six connected sets, and the absence of edge deletion makes A–B anticompleteness necessary. Conversely those operations produce exactly K6 minus AB. Seven labels enumerate every possible certificate, and all conditions are checkable in O(n²) per labeling.
claims.witness: The six labeled connected sets themselves are an NP certificate; contracting each set yields the required six-vertex quotient.
claims.search_method: Derived both implications directly from vertex deletion and edge contraction, checking all fourteen required branch-pair adjacencies and the unique forbidden pair.

claims.claim: Bounded-skeleton structural reduction: G contains K6 minus an edge as an induced minor if and only if it has six nonempty pairwise vertex-disjoint tree subgraphs TA,TB,T1,T2,T3,T4 and one selected cross-edge for each of the fourteen target edges, with no edge of G between TA and TB. The exceptional trees TA,TB may be chosen with at most four leaves and at most two vertices of tree-degree at least three; every core tree Ti may be chosen with at most five leaves and at most three vertices of tree-degree at least three. After suppressing unmarked degree-two vertices there are at most 44 essential vertices in total, and hence only finitely many marked skeleton types.
claims.evidence: For each branch, choose one endpoint for every incident selected cross-edge and take a minimal subtree spanning those marked vertices. Every leaf is marked. A nontrivial tree with ℓ leaves has at most ℓ−2 vertices of degree at least three. Target degrees are four for A,B and five for each Ci, giving the asserted leaf and branching bounds. Essential-vertex bounds are therefore 2·(4+2)+4·(5+3)=44. Restriction preserves all selected edges and A–B anticompleteness, while the converse follows from the certificate in claim 0.
claims.witness: The minimal marked subtrees obtained from any branch model, together with one selected edge for each target adjacency, give the bounded skeleton.
claims.search_method: Checked singleton and nontrivial subtree cases separately, applied the exact tree degree identity, summed all six bounds, and verified the converse contraction.

claims.claim: Let q be the number of nonedges of G. Detection is fixed-parameter tractable in q, in time O(7^(2q+3)n²), and undecided instances have at most 2q+3 vertices. In particular, the problem is polynomial-time solvable when q=O(log n).
claims.evidence: A complete graph is negative. If q>0 and four universal vertices exist, any nonedge endpoints plus four universal vertices induce K6 minus that edge. Otherwise there are at most three universal vertices, and every other vertex is an endpoint of at least one of the q nonedges, so n≤2q+3. Applying claim 0's enumeration on the retained instance gives the stated FPT bound; q=O(log n) makes its exponential factor polynomial in n.
claims.witness: In the immediate yes case, the witness is any nonedge xy together with four universal vertices; in the residual case, the 2q nonedge incidences cover every nonuniversal vertex.
claims.search_method: Proved the universal-vertex dichotomy symbolically and exhaustively checked its alternatives on all 2,131,019 labeled graphs of orders at most seven.

claims.claim: On chordal graphs, K6 minus an edge is an induced minor if and only if it is already an induced subgraph. Thus chordal inputs can be decided in O(n^6) time by enumerating six vertices. The same argument works for Kt minus an edge for every fixed t≥3.
claims.evidence: The four core branches give four internally vertex-disjoint A–B paths, so an inclusion-minimal A–B separator S disjoint from A∪B has size at least four. In a chordal graph such a minimal separator is a clique and the A-side and B-side full components each contain an S-complete vertex. The latter follows by maximizing the S-neighborhood of a component vertex; a shortest path to any missed separator vertex otherwise creates an induced cycle or a vertex with a larger S-neighborhood. Choosing four vertices of S and one S-complete vertex from each side induces exactly K6 minus one edge. Replacing four by t−2 proves the fixed-t statement.
claims.witness: Four vertices of the clique separator S, together with S-complete vertices x and y in its two full components, induce K6 minus xy.
claims.search_method: Reproved the separator and full-component lemmas and exhaustively enumerated all 617,675 labeled chordal graphs on seven vertices; among 4,466 positive induced-minor instances, none lacked the induced subgraph.

claims.claim: There is an explicit polynomial-time classification on complete multipartite graphs. Let the part sizes be n1,…,nr. For every i with ni≥2, reserve two vertices of part i and put mi=ni−2 and mj=nj for j≠i. Accept exactly when, for some s∈{0,…,4} and some s distinct indices J⊆{1,…,r}\{i}, subtracting one from each mj with j∈J leaves counts whose complete multipartite graph has a matching of size at least 4−s. If the residual total is M and its largest part has size L, this matching size is min(⌊M/2⌋,M−L).
claims.evidence: Two anticomplete connected exceptional branches must be distinct singleton vertices in one part. Each core branch is either a singleton in a distinct outside part or spans at least two parts and can be reduced to a cross-part edge. Such edge branches are mutually adjacent and adjacent to every outside-part singleton, so the remaining requirement is exactly a matching of size 4−s in the residual multipartite graph. Its maximum matching size is min(⌊M/2⌋,M−L), from the total-vertex and largest-part bounds, both simultaneously attainable by cross-part pairing.
claims.witness: A successful tuple (i,s,J) gives the two reserved exceptional singletons, s singleton core branches, and 4−s residual matching edges as the other core branches.
claims.search_method: Proved necessity and sufficiency by branch shrinking and compared the formula against a generic exhaustive branch-set search for all 96 complete-multipartite isomorphism types of order at most nine.

claims.claim: Given a tree decomposition of width w, detection is decidable in n·2^{O(w log w)} time; hence it is polynomial-time solvable on every fixed-width class supplied with such decompositions.
claims.evidence: A nice-decomposition dynamic program can store a seven-way bag labeling, a connectivity partition refining each nonunused label, constant-size unseen/active/completed flags, and fourteen adjacency bits. Forget and join transitions enforce that no disconnected component of a label disappears or is restarted, and edge transitions record required adjacencies while rejecting A–B edges. The number of states is at most 7^(w+1)·Bell(w+1) times a constant, and even quadratic state pairing at joins remains 2^{O(w log w)}.
claims.witness: An accepting root state has six completed nonempty connected labels, all fourteen required adjacency bits, and no forbidden A–B edge.
claims.search_method: Audited introduce, edge, forget, join, and root cases and independently counted the labeled connectivity partitions.

claims.claim: A model cannot in general be normalized so that either endpoint of the missing edge has a singleton branch set. A 12-vertex counterexample consists of anticomplete paths A=a1a2a3a4 and B=b1b2b3b4, a clique C={c1,c2,c3,c4}, and exactly the additional edges aici and bici for i=1,…,4.
claims.evidence: The two paths and four clique singletons form a model. A singleton exceptional branch needs four distinct neighbors, so it must be some ci. Its anticomplete mate is then an interval in a component of A−ai or B−bi. Symmetry reduces to i=1,2. For i=2 every such interval has fewer than four external neighbors. For i=1, the only four-neighbor intervals force a core branch to contain a1, which is isolated after the two exceptional branches are removed and therefore cannot be adjacent to the other three cores.
claims.witness: The stated 12-vertex graph is positive via branches A,B,{c1},{c2},{c3},{c4}, but admits no model with a singleton exceptional branch.
claims.search_method: Checked the boundary-neighborhood cases analytically and exhaustively searched every connected branch-set model having one singleton exceptional branch.

claims.claim: For every integer L≥1 there is a graph G_L on 6L+6 vertices that contains K6 minus an edge as an induced minor, but in every model each of the two branch sets corresponding to the missing-edge endpoints has at least L+1 vertices. Hence no universal constant bounds either exceptional branch set in all models.
claims.evidence: Subdividing each of the six path edges into length L gives 6L+6 vertices and preserves the evident model. If an exceptional branch contains clique vertices indexed by nonempty I, its anticomplete mate is an interval avoiding the I-indexed marks. After restoring all nonclique vertices of the first branch, the component containing the remaining clique has at most 4−|I|≤3 neighbors of that interval, and every other component has at most one. This contradicts the four core branches, whose connected union lies in one component and supplies four distinct neighbors. Thus both exceptional branches are path intervals. Such an interval has at most two boundary neighbors plus one clique neighbor per contained mark; four distinct core neighbors force two marks, hence at least L+1 vertices.
claims.witness: G_L consists of two four-mark paths with every consecutive-mark distance L, a K4 on c1,…,c4, and spokes from ci to the ith mark of both paths.
claims.search_method: Proved the component-neighbor bound for arbitrary L and exactly checked 1,748,240 clique-exception component cases plus 206,720 interval cases for every L from 1 through 40.

claims.claim: Sharp obstruction at minimum width: for every L≥1, the graph G_L in the preceding claim has treewidth exactly 4 and order n=6L+6, while every model has each missing-edge endpoint branch set of size at least n/6. Hence even on treewidth-4 inputs—the minimum treewidth of any positive instance—no o(n) universal bound can be imposed on either exceptional branch set.
claims.evidence: Claim 7 gives L+1=(6L+6)/6=n/6. Eliminating each subdivided path from its first mark to its fourth gives at most four later neighbors at every step; eliminating the final K4 therefore witnesses treewidth at most four. Contracting either whole path produces a K5 with c1,…,c4, proving treewidth at least four. Every positive instance has treewidth at least four because K6 minus an edge contains K5 and induced-minor containment implies ordinary-minor containment. The linear lower bound along this family excludes every o(n) normalization.
claims.witness: The path-first elimination ordering has width four, while one contracted path together with the four clique vertices is a K5 minor certificate.
claims.search_method: Verified the universal upper and lower bounds symbolically and exactly simulated the claimed elimination order and contraction witness for L=1,…,40.

target_evidence: The source target requests an unrestricted complexity classification for detecting K6 minus one edge as an induced minor and, if tractable, a polynomial-time algorithm. The draft supplies correct certificate, structural, parameterized, special-class, and obstruction results, but neither an unrestricted polynomial-time algorithm nor an unrestricted hardness proof. These are material advances but do not completely resolve the target. Its explicit PARTIAL label and unrestricted-coverage disclaimer are accurate.
